newsitem.title: INDIA: Vote on Mother Teresa's successor postponed.
newsitem.headline: Vote on Mother Teresa's successor postponed.

text.p: The election to choose a successor to Mother Teresa at the head of the Missionaries of Charity religious order has been postponed from February 2, the Roman Catholic church said on Tuesday.

The office of Archbishop of Calcutta Henry D'Souza gave no explanation for the postponement and did not set a new date for the election. It said the ailing 86-year-old nun had agreed to the postponement.
"The election of the Superior General of the Missionaries of Charity Sisters will not be held on February 2, 1997, as previously foreseen," the archbishop's secretariat said.

"The General Chapter will enter into the deliberations first," it said, referring to the 103-member electoral college formed to name a successor to the order's founder. "Mother Teresa has given her consent to this request."

More than 100 nuns began a two-week retreat on January 16 to select a successor to the 1979 Nobel Peace Prize winner, who has been taken to hospital three times since August, twice for heart trouble and once after hitting her head in a fall.

Set to end on January 31, the retreat was to be followed by several meetings of the General Chapter before the election by secret ballot next Sunday, but a Missionaries of Charity spokeswoman indicated the retreat was being extended.

"The nuns are now in seminar...They are taking time in the seminar. It's very important for us. We can't tell you when it will end and when the deliberations of the General Chapter will start," the spokeswoman said.

The 1979 Nobel Peace Prize winner, known affectionately as "Mother", had wanted to step down in 1990, one year after she was fitted with a heart pacemaker, because of ill health. But her colleagues asked her to stay on.
Mother Teresa has led the order since the start, shaping the mission's work in 111 countries with her strong, charismatic personality.
But she has decided to retire as the order's superior general because of heart, kidney and lung problems.
"Mother Teresa does not want to continue as superior general because of her poor health and a weak heart," a Missionaries of Charity spokeswoman said earlier this month.
A regular six-year election by secret ballot set for last September had to be delayed because Mother Teresa was sent to hospital in August with heart problems, pneumonia and malaria.
The Missionaries of Charity spokeswoman said Mother Teresa's health was stable. "She is much better now although she is still weak," she said.
The selection process which began earlier this month involves the 103 members of the order's electoral college, or General Chapter.
The college is comprised of representatives from various sections of the order, which has about 4,500 nuns.
The retreat was being held at the order's headquarters, Mother's House, in the eastern city of Calcutta for the first time to allow Mother Teresa to participate.
Asked if he had any idea when the secret ballot would not be held, Father Edward Le Joly, a spiritual adviser to the Missionaries of Charity, said: "I have got no idea when it's going to be held."
